reverse_outline.summary: What the part builds: the six discovery components, from index to alerts
Business stake: discovery surfaces start contacts and decide which listings are seen and whether paid visibility pays
Architect stake: busiest read paths, whose indices teams are tempted to treat as the system of record | discovery couples taxonomy, events, ML and monetization on every query
Three key claims: surfaces are rebuildable read models that remove sold listings fast; structured filters beat clever models; ordering is an owned, versioned policy judged on contacts
Three failure patterns the part counters (search as system of record, multiplier creep, ghost inventory) and the fix for each
Hand-off from Part III's clean supply to the buyer side | listing discovery behaves like a high-write operational system, not web search
Thesis: discovery is one pipeline with six surfaces sharing one stream and taxonomy, each answering the same three questions (available, who set position, did it lead to contact)
Roadmap: why the chapters come in this order, each surface building on the previous
Lead-in to the chapter table of questions and when to read each
Dependencies on earlier parts and constraints/inputs from later parts (trust gate, paid placements, platform)

Veldmark's January 2027 reindex brownout showing the cost of a non-rebuildable index | the 2027 decisions per surface (shared OpenSearch platform, ranking policy v1, carousel rebuild, geo compiler, saved-search service)
Synthesis: answering the three questions once for the whole pipeline, what the reader should be able to say, and pointer to start with search architecture

results.quote: Recommendations reuse ranking's machinery without a query, map search compiles places as query understanding compiles words, and alerts come last because they reuse every surface before them.
results.finding: The stated rule is that each chapter builds on the one before, but map search's reason ties it to query understanding, not recommendations, so its fifth position stays unexplained. The draft gives exactly the spec's reason; the difficulty lies in the declared order/rationale.

results.quote: The argument of this part is that discovery is **one pipeline with six surfaces**, not six products.

results.quote: decide on one change for each surface except query understanding
